subject: people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
tagline: Coinbase for people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
one_liner: A qualified custodian for the one that got away.
brand_voice_notes: Trust-company gravity applied to feelings a healthy person processed in 2009. Closure speaks exclusively in securities language: memories are deposits, regret is yield, the sweetheart is a ticker. It never acknowledges that any of this is sad. 2009 is referred to only as a fiscal year. Compliance is invoked constantly and protects no one. The word 'love' does not appear in any filing.

hero.h1: The one that got away is now an asset class.
hero.sub: Closure is a regulated exchange for positions you opened in high school and never closed. Deposit the memories. Watch the chart. Do not text them.

features.title: The Sweetheart Index (SWTH)
features.blurb: One ticker tracking your high school sweetheart's publicly visible life trajectory: the promotion, the lake house, the boat. Updated nightly from sources they forgot were public. Our most-checked chart, by a margin our analysts describe as concerning.

features.title: Cold Storage
features.blurb: Prom photos, ticket stubs, and the mix CD from 2007, hashed and vaulted in a facility in rural Nevada. Retrieval takes six to eight weeks and a notarized statement explaining what, exactly, you plan to do with them.

features.title: Regret Staking
features.blurb: Lock your what-ifs for twenty-five years and earn 4.1% APY, compounded on anniversaries. Early withdrawal is permitted once per decade and triggers a courtesy call to your mother.

demo_screen_concept: A brokerage terminal for a single holding: SWTH, the Sweetheart Index. Main panel is a line chart of the sweetheart's perceived life trajectory rendered as an engraved statistical plate, with range toggles (1D, 1W, 1Y, SINCE PROM) that redraw the line, and event annotations pinned to the curve ('Got the boat', 'Second marriage', 'Ran the half-marathon'). Right sidebar: current holdings ledger (WHATIF, APLGY, MIXTP) with cost basis and unrealized sentiment, plus a staked position showing a 25-year lock countdown. A Buy panel accepts an amount and opens a confirmation modal that restates the purchase in compliance language; the Sell button is permanently disabled with a tooltip reading 'Markets close at 11pm for your protection.' Bottom strip: a watchlist of other people's sweethearts, each row marked WAITLISTED.

images.rationale: Hero skipped: the design direction is a typographic engraved-certificate composition with a CSS guilloché specimen plate, so a photo would fight the intaglio system. Demo assets skipped: the demo is a chart/ledger brokerage terminal, not photo-shaped. Full budget went to three testimonial portraits, art-directed as banknote-engraving vignettes in the entry's single green ink so they read as printed on the certificate rather than pasted onto it.

design_direction.style: Engraved-securities prospectus, banknote-intaglio daylight mode. The page is staged as the offering document of a heavily funded digital-asset custodian that has decided unresolved adolescent attachment is a bearer instrument and prices acceptance by the position. A bearer-bond ivory ground carries the visual system of a 19th-century trust company that now clears crypto: every panel is a certificate plate with a double-rule border (a 2px outer rule and a 1px inner rule with a small gap, all in intaglio green), square corners, no shadows of any kind; depth comes entirely from rule weight, ivory-on-ivory panel fills, and engraved ornament. Guilloché does the illustration: rosette medallions built from CSS repeating-conic-gradients and layered ring borders sit where a bank would put its seal, and thin repeating-linear-gradient security hatching fills panel margins and section dividers, so the page reads as printed security paper rather than a website. Certificate chrome annotates everything: serial numbers in the corners of plates (NO. 002009), 'PAYABLE TO BEARER' microcopy, ruled ledger tables with tabular figures. One intaglio hunter green carries the wordmark, headlines, rules, ornament, and all institutional text, so the whole instrument reads as engraved in a single ink; one rationed wax-seal burgundy is reserved strictly for the single primary CTA per section (ivory text on burgundy fill), the live custody-status dot, and the SWTH downtick, and appears almost nowhere else. Playfair Display sets the wordmark and headlines in high-contrast engraved serif with the confidence of a bank older than your feelings; Public Sans carries plain, faintly regulatory body copy, because the modern half of the company writes like a federal filing. Every figure that pretends to be custody telemetry (index levels, APY, cost bases, lock countdowns, tier prices) is set in Fira Mono with tabular figures inside ruled ledger wells, so it reads like a statement, not marketing. Motion is engraver-restrained: the custody dot pulses on a 3s cycle, the SWTH line draws itself once on load, plates fade up 6px on scroll with a 40ms stagger, the CTA depresses 1px on press like a seal, ledger digits tick once on reveal, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no clay, no bento cells, no offset brutalist shadows, no gradients used as color (only as engraving texture), no postal or stamp motifs, no marquee, no emoji. Reads like an institution that files heartbreak under 'unrealized losses' and considers 2009 an open tax year.

design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split certificate: left column carries a small 'FORM CL-2009' kicker, the giant Playfair h1, the regulatory sub, and the burgundy Begin custody CTA; right column is a framed specimen certificate plate with guilloché rosette, serial number, 'ONE (1) UNRESOLVED POSITION' denomination, and a live SWTH quote in a ledger well. Double-rule certificate border wraps the whole hero.
